opex.name: Operating, selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the stores, clubs, warehouses and head office.

follow100Note: The stores earned $3.86 of operating profit from every $100 of revenue, but a $4,750M unrealized loss on investment stakes — inside the 'Other income' line above — plus tax and partners' shares left just $0.28. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net profit shown is the $453M attributable to Walmart; consolidated net income was $643M, of which $190M belongs to noncontrolling interests. Per-share figures are shown split-adjusted for the 3-for-1 stock split distributed February 23, 2024; as originally reported before the split, GAAP EPS was $0.17 and adjusted EPS was $1.53.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: split-adjusted; $0.17 as reported pre-split; adjusted $0.51 split-adjusted ($1.53 pre-split)

oneTimers: Other (gains) and losses was a $4,750M loss this quarter — unrealized fair-value declines on equity and other investments Walmart holds. Adjusted EPS of $1.53 (as reported before the split) excludes the loss's $1.36-per-share effect, net of tax.

The year-ago quarter's operating expenses included a large opioid-litigation charge, which flatters this quarter's reported comparisons: operating expenses as a share of net sales fell 182 basis points, and reported operating income rose 130.1% against 3.0% on an adjusted basis.
otherDetail: Net interest expense of $537M, plus a $4,750M loss in 'Other (gains) and losses' — unrealized fair-value declines on equity and other investments Walmart holds.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: Stores and eCommerce in the United States — comparable sales rose 4.9% excluding fuel, eCommerce rose 24%, and segment operating income was $4,981M.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores and eCommerce outside the U.S. — net sales rose 5.4% in constant currency, led by Walmex and China; growth was muted by the timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days, which shifted into the fourth quarter. Segment operating income was $1,117M.

segments.name: Sam's Club U.S.
segments.note: Walmart's warehouse clubs in the United States — comparable sales rose 3.8% excluding fuel, eCommerce rose 16%, membership income rose 7.2%, and segment operating income was $593M.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Membership fees from Sam's Club and Walmart+, plus other income — small, but nearly cost-free.

takeaways.text: Walmart U.S. comparable sales rose 4.9% excluding fuel, with transactions up 3.4% and eCommerce up 24%; global eCommerce rose 15% and the global advertising business about 20%, with Walmart Connect up 26%.
takeaways.title: U.S. stores stayed strong

takeaways.text: A $4,750M loss on equity and other investments — unrealized fair-value moves on stakes Walmart holds — held GAAP profit to $453M. Adjusted EPS, which strips the loss out, was $1.53 as reported ($0.51 split-adjusted).
takeaways.title: A paper loss swamped the stores

takeaways.text: Walmart raised its fiscal 2024 outlook to net sales growth of 5.0–5.5% and adjusted EPS of $6.40–$6.48. Reported operating income rose 130.1% to $6,202M — flattered by a charge-hit year-ago quarter; adjusted operating income rose 3.0%.
takeaways.title: Guidance raised

verdict: Walmart grew revenue 5.2% to $160.8B on 4.9% U.S. comparable sales and 15% global eCommerce growth, and raised its full-year guidance — but a $4.75B unrealized loss on its investment stakes held headline profit to $453M, while adjusted EPS was $1.53.
